brief: The canvas displays a vast, deep-time geological cross-section, presenting layered stripes of poured concrete. Massive canyon walls rise and recede as the scene depicts the slow, constant cycle of sedimentation. These layers shift and build up within the visible area, showing the inescapable process of material deposition over eons. The concrete surface maintains a uniform palette of earthen tones, moving perpetually as the strata gather and solidify in a breathtaking, unavoidable geological rhythm.

statement: This sketch depicts a vast geological cross-section revealing the slow, continuous process of sedimentation in a deep-time canyon. The composition shows layered deposits of poured concrete in earth tones—brown, tan, and gray—stacked vertically to represent millions of years of material accumulation. These layers shift gently over time, simulating the constant, inevitable rhythm of deposition, with subtle movements and erosion effects that suggest the dynamic nature of geological processes. The canyon walls frame this view, emphasizing the immense scale of time and the enduring power of natural forces.
